newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crop production Dec 12 highlights - USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crop production Dec 12 highlights - USDA.

text.p: U.S. soybean and wheat supplies will remain tight for months to come, the Agriculture Department said Thursday, forecasting carryover stocks of 180 million bushels of soybeans and 435 million bushels of wheat.
For corn, 1996/97 ending stocks of 1.157 billion bushels were estimated. Heavy demand at home and abroad was expected to gobble up this year's harvests and keep prices strong.

Corn exports were pegged at 1.900 billion bushels, soybeans at 900 million and wheat at 950 million. A month ago, the figures were 1.950 billion bushels for corn, 870 million for soybeans and 950 million for wheat.
X-Cotton production in 1,000 bales, yield in lbs per acre.
The estimate for corn stocks was up slightly due to lower exports, soybean stocks were down and wheat stocks unchanged.

In its December crop report, USDA pegged the cotton crop at 18.738 million bales, the third largest ever, and up slightly from November due to good conditions. Exports were estimated at 6.20 million bales and ending stocks at 4.60 million.
Florida orange production was forecast for 220.0 million boxes and the orange juice yield at 1.53 gallons per box.
With the harvest season ending, corn output was put at 9.265 billion bushels, soybeans at 2.403 billion and wheat at 2.282 billion, unchanged from November's estimates.
Y-Cotton ending stocks and exports in million 480-lb bales.
